title: Verify generated code: independent oracles and mutation checks
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects verify generated code: independent oracles and mutation checks with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Candidate acceptance includes executable results, rejected mutations, reviewed dependencies and a human explanation of tradeoffs.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Generated code can import nonexistent APIs, mishandle edge cases or encode the wrong requirement. A compile/type check establishes basic structural compatibility, not correctness. Unit tests check isolated behavior; integration tests check real contracts; static and dependency checks address additional risks.
The model that wrote a function should not be the only authority judging it. Use independent requirements, trusted fixtures and known counterexamples as test oracles.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Run format/lint/type checks, targeted unit tests and integration tests in a sandbox before review. Inspect dependencies and API versions against official documentation. Keep secrets and production services unavailable to candidate code.

Mutation testing changes a relevant operator or return value and checks whether the suite fails. A surviving mutation reveals a possible assertion gap, though equivalent mutations need review. For a generated classifier, mutate category mapping and UNKNOWN handling.
sections.code:
def allowed(role):return role=='admin'
assert allowed('admin') and not allowed('viewer')

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A generated test copies the same faulty formula as the implementation, so both agree. Another test asserts only that a function returns something. A hallucinated library import fails only after deployment because no import smoke test ran.
Use boundary values, negative cases and independently computed expectations. Review failing mutations by requirement, and ensure the suite catches permission bypasses as well as numerical errors.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Candidate acceptance includes executable results, rejected mutations, reviewed dependencies and a human explanation of tradeoffs. Keep generated provenance for audit but evaluate quality by the same standards as handwritten code.
SDETs should distinguish a generator's confidence from test evidence. Code is accepted when independent checks demonstrate the specified behavior, not when a model claims it is production ready.

mistake: A generated test copies the same faulty formula as the implementation, so both agree. Another test asserts only that a function returns something. A hallucinated library import fails only after deployment because no import smoke test ran.
takeaway: Candidate acceptance includes executable results, rejected mutations, reviewed dependencies and a human explanation of tradeoffs.

title: Generated dependencies: import checks and sandbox boundaries
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects generated dependencies: import checks and sandbox boundaries with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance combines compatible dependencies, meaningful behavior tests, reviewed effects and actual isolation appropriate to the environment.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A generated function can rely on a nonexistent library or an obsolete method even when the algorithm sounds correct. Dependency manifests, lockfiles, import smoke tests and official API checks establish compatibility. Static inspection can identify suspicious calls, but it is not a complete sandbox.
Generated candidates must run without production credentials, with resource limits and controlled network/filesystem access. A model's instruction to behave safely does not isolate the process.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Parse Python with ast before execution, review imports and reject unsupported dependencies. Run type/compile checks and focused tests in a disposable environment. Lock accepted versions and inspect transitive dependency advisories.

AST-based rules can detect direct eval/exec or os.system calls for review, but aliases, dynamic imports and indirect effects can evade simple patterns. Use operating-system/container isolation for enforcement and label lexical/static checks as screening.
sections.code:
import ast
tree=ast.parse('import imaginary_package')
imports=[n.names[0].name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n,ast.Import)]
assert imports==['imaginary_package']

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A test suite never imports the generated module, so a hallucinated import remains hidden. A deny list blocks the string subprocess while a dynamically assembled command still executes. Installing every generated dependency expands supply-chain risk.

Test import failure and API mismatch explicitly. Keep an allowlisted dependency set for candidate tasks, and inspect a deliberately evasive example to understand why screening cannot guarantee containment.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance combines compatible dependencies, meaningful behavior tests, reviewed effects and actual isolation appropriate to the environment. The browser worker limits runtime and keeps credentials absent; local code needs its own controlled execution environment.

For SDETs, distinguish test discovery from execution: a file can exist without its assertions ever running. Verify a known failing candidate makes the pipeline fail before trusting generated-code coverage.

mistake: A test suite never imports the generated module, so a hallucinated import remains hidden. A deny list blocks the string subprocess while a dynamically assembled command still executes. Installing every generated dependency expands supply-chain risk.
takeaway: Acceptance combines compatible dependencies, meaningful behavior tests, reviewed effects and actual isolation appropriate to the environment.

assert imports_in('x=1')==[]
